name: Chicken adobo
description: Chicken braised in soy sauce with vinegar, garlic and bay. The vinegar is left unstirred for the first ten minutes.

instructions.text: Marinate the chicken in the soy with the crushed garlic and peppercorns for thirty minutes.
Lift the chicken out, dry it and brown it skin down. Keep the marinade.
Pour in the marinade, water and vinegar, add the bay and sugar. Bring it to the boil and neither stir nor cover for ten minutes.
Cover and simmer for twenty-five minutes, turning the chicken once.
Uncover and reduce the sauce for five to ten minutes, spooning it over the chicken. Serve with rice.

name: Baleadas
description: A wheat flour tortilla folded over refried beans, soured cream and crumbled cheese.

instructions.text: Rub the flour with the fat and salt to a crumb, add the hot water and knead a soft dough.
Divide it into eight balls, oil them and rest them twenty minutes under a cloth.
Fry the onion in oil, add the cooked beans with some of their liquid and mash them smooth.
Fry the purée over medium heat for ten minutes, until it holds its shape on a spoon.
Roll the balls into thin twenty-centimetre rounds.
Cook them on a hot dry pan a minute a side, to spotted but not dried out.
Spread beans over half the tortilla, add cream and cheese, fold it over and serve hot.

name: Grilled barramundi
description: A whole fish on the grate with lemon myrtle and lime, part in foil and part over direct heat.

instructions.text: Cut three slashes on each side of the fish and pat it completely dry.
Work the garlic with the butter, lemon myrtle, lime zest, salt and pepper.
Rub the mixture into the slashes and the cavity and tuck slices of lime and fennel inside.
Wrap the fish in foil with the seams on top so the juices do not run out.
Light the coals and rake them to the sides; the heat under the fish has to be indirect.
Cook it in the foil for twenty minutes, turning the parcel once halfway.
Unwrap it, move the fish onto an oiled grate over the coals and give it a minute a side for the crust.

name: Beef Stroganoff
description: Beef cut into strips and seared hard, in a soured cream sauce with onion.

instructions.text: Cut the beef across the grain into centimetre strips, pat them dry and pepper them.
Heat a pan hard and sear the beef in batches for ninety seconds, without turning it often.
Lift out the meat and fry the mushrooms over a high flame until their water has gone.
Add the butter and onion and fry until soft and golden.
Stir in the flour, cook it a minute and add the stock, stirring until smooth.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the soured cream and mustard, and season.
Return the meat with its juices, warm it a minute without boiling and scatter with parsley.

name: Bibimbap
description: Rice under separately cooked vegetables, meat and an egg, mixed with gochujang right before eating.

instructions.text: Marinate the beef in soy, garlic and a spoon of sesame oil for twenty minutes.
Blanch the spinach for thirty seconds, squeeze it dry and dress with sesame oil and a pinch of salt. Boil the sprouts three minutes and dress them the same way, with garlic.
Fry the carrot and the mushrooms separately, a couple of minutes each, seasoning each on its own. No need to wash the pan in between.
Sear the beef over a high flame for two minutes. Fry the eggs separately, leaving the yolks runny.
Divide the hot rice between bowls, arrange the vegetables and beef in sections, and top with an egg and a spoon of gochujang. Each person does the mixing.

name: Bircher muesli
description: Oats soaked overnight with grated apple, cream and nuts.

instructions.text: Cover the oats with water or apple juice and leave them overnight in the fridge.
In the morning stir in the yoghurt, cream and condensed milk until even.
Grate the apples, skins and all, on a coarse grater straight into the bowl.
Squeeze lemon juice over the grated apple at once and stir it through so it does not brown.
Toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan for five minutes and chop them coarsely.
Stir in the honey, divide it between bowls and top with the nuts and berries.

name: Brik
description: A thin sheet of pastry with an egg inside, fried so the yolk stays liquid.

instructions.text: Mix the mashed potato with the tuna, chopped onion, capers, parsley, harissa, salt and pepper.
Heat the oil to 180 °C. Test with a scrap of pastry: it should surface at once and sizzle.
Lay a sheet on a plate, put two spoons of filling on one half and make a hollow in it.
Break an egg into the hollow, season it and fold the sheet over immediately, pressing the edges.
Slide the brik into the oil and fry forty seconds a side, steadying it with a slotted spoon.
Drain on paper and serve immediately with a wedge of lemon.

name: Casado
description: A lunch plate of rice, beans, salad, plantain and meat, each in its own sector.

instructions.text: Marinate the chicken in lime juice, garlic, Salsa Lizano, salt and pepper for twenty minutes.
Cook the rice loose and warm the beans with a spoon of their liquid.
Dice the chayote and carrot small and stew them with garlic for ten minutes; that is the picadillo.
Fry the chicken over medium heat, six minutes a side.
Fry the ripe plantain slices to a caramel colour.
Toss the shredded cabbage with tomato, coriander, lime juice and salt.
Build the plate in sectors: rice, beans, chicken, picadillo, salad, plantain — unmixed.

name: Chakhokhbili
description: Chicken stewed without water in its own juices with tomatoes and a mountain of fresh herbs.

instructions.text: Brown the chicken pieces in a dry heavy pot without fat, to a golden crust.
Lift out the meat, add the butter and soften the onion in the rendered fat.
Skin the tomatoes, grate them and add them to the onion.
Return the chicken, season, add the khmeli suneli and the whole chilli and cover the pot.
Stew thirty minutes on a low heat, never adding water.
Chop all the herbs and the garlic coarsely, not to a paste.
Stir in the herbs and garlic, cover the pot, take it off the heat and let it stand ten minutes.

name: Chakka
description: Strained cultured cheese with herbs and garlic, the Tajik spread for flatbread.

instructions.text: Line a colander with two layers of close-woven cloth and pour in the katyk.
Knot the corners of the cloth and hang the bundle over a bowl somewhere cold.
Leave it draining a full day, until the mass is as firm as soft curd.
Pound the garlic with a pinch of salt into a smooth paste.
Chop the coriander, dill, basil and spring onion as fine as you can.
Fold the herbs and garlic into the strained mass with a spatula, without mashing it.
Salt it, smooth it in a bowl, press a hollow with a spoon and pour the oil into it.

name: Dal bhat
description: Lentil soup with rice and a vegetable tarkari. Nepal's everyday meal, eaten twice a day for a lifetime.

instructions.text: Rinse the lentils and boil them in a litre of water with the turmeric for thirty minutes, until they collapse completely. Skim for the first five minutes.
Start the rice. While it cooks, fry the onion, add the potato and cauliflower with a little turmeric and water, and cook fifteen minutes: that is the tarkari.
Fry the greens with garlic over a high flame for two minutes; they should stay bright.
For the jhaneko, heat the ghee and throw in the ajwain, cumin, dried chilli and garlic, frying twenty seconds to the smell.
Pour the sizzling spiced fat straight into the dal — it hisses. Stir, season and serve at once.
Build the plate: rice in the middle, dal in a small bowl, tarkari and greens around it, achar at the edge.

name: Piri-piri chicken
description: Chicken spatchcocked and grilled over coals under a sauce of piri-piri, garlic and lemon.

instructions.text: Cut the chicken along the backbone, open it out and press it flat.
Blend the chillies, garlic, the juice of two lemons, paprika, vinegar, oregano, oil and salt.
Pour half the sauce into a separate bowl; that half is for basting.
Coat the chicken with the rest, working it under the skin, and refrigerate overnight.
Light the coals and rake them to the sides; the heat has to be indirect.
Grill the chicken skin up for thirty minutes, then turn it and give it fifteen more.
For the last five minutes baste with the reserved sauce mixed with melted butter. Serve with lemon.

name: Gallo pinto
description: Yesterday's rice fried with black beans and Salsa Lizano. The Costa Rican breakfast, every day.

instructions.text: Fry the finely chopped onion, pepper and garlic in oil until soft, five minutes.
Add the beans with a ladle of their liquid and warm them three minutes.
Add the cold rice and stir, breaking up lumps with a spatula.
Add the Salsa Lizano, season and fry over medium heat for seven minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the chopped coriander and take it off the heat.
Serve with fried eggs, fried plantain and, if you like, soured cream or fresh cheese.

name: Gong bao chicken
description: Diced chicken with peanuts and dried chillies in a sauce where the vinegar matters more than the sugar.

instructions.text: Mix the chicken with the egg white, a spoon of cornflour, a spoon of soy and a pinch of salt, and leave it twenty minutes.
Mix the sauce in advance: vinegar, the rest of the soy, the sugar and the rest of the cornflour with two spoons of water. Keep it within reach — there is no time to mix it later.
Heat the oil and fry the chillies with the Sichuan pepper for twenty seconds, until dark but not black. Burnt chilli turns bitter.
Add the chicken and leave it alone for a minute, then toss and cook through — two minutes more.
Throw in the garlic, ginger and the white of the spring onion, then after half a minute pour in the sauce. It thickens in seconds. Off the heat, add the peanuts and the green of the onion.

name: Gyudon
description: Thinly sliced beef simmered with onion in dashi, soy and mirin, over rice.

instructions.text: Bring the dashi with the soy, mirin, sake, sugar and grated ginger to the boil in a wide pan.
Add the onion and simmer for five minutes over medium heat, until it turns translucent.
Lay the beef over the surface slice by slice rather than in a heap, and cook two or three minutes. Skim any foam.
Take it off the moment the beef loses its pink. Left longer it toughens within a minute.
Divide the rice between bowls, spoon the beef and onion over with two or three spoons of the broth, and serve with the pickled ginger.

name: Grilled halloumi with watermelon
description: Cypriot cheese seared to a crust, with cold watermelon and mint. The island's summer plate.

instructions.text: Soak the halloumi in cold water for fifteen minutes, drain it and pat it completely dry.
Cut the cheese into centimetre slices — thinner and it dries out, thicker and it will not heat through.
Cut the chilled watermelon into large cubes and keep it in the fridge until serving.
Heat a dry pan hard and sear the halloumi two minutes a side, to dark stripes.
Whisk the olive oil with the lemon juice, honey and pepper.
Arrange the watermelon, rocket and hot cheese, spoon over the dressing and scatter with mint. Serve at once.

name: Jasha maroo
description: Chopped chicken in a thin broth with ginger, garlic and chilli. Bhutanese everyday cooking.

instructions.text: Chop the chicken through the bone into pieces about the size of a matchbox.

Fry the onion in oil until soft, add the paste and cook it two minutes.

Add the tomatoes and chillies, pour in water a finger above and season.
Simmer twenty minutes; the broth should stay thin.
Stir in the coriander and serve in deep bowls with red rice.

name: Joojeh kabab
description: Chicken in a saffron marinade with onion juice and lemon, grilled over coals.

instructions.text: Grind the saffron with a pinch of sugar and steep it in three spoons of warm water for fifteen minutes.
Grate the onions finely and squeeze the juice through muslin, discarding the pulp.
Mix the onion juice, half the saffron infusion, the juice of two lemons, the yoghurt, oil, salt and pepper.
Cut the chicken into four-centimetre pieces, coat it in the marinade and refrigerate it eight hours.
Thread the pieces onto flat skewers packed tight and get the coals to an even strong heat.
Grill eight minutes a side, turning the skewer every two minutes.
Mix the melted butter with the remaining saffron and brush the kebabs before serving. Serve with rice, tomatoes and sumac.

name: Köttbullar
description: Meatballs on a panade of bread and cream, in a cream sauce, with lingonberry and mashed potato.

instructions.text: Soak the bread in a hundred millilitres of the cream for ten minutes and mash it to a paste.
Fry the onion in butter until soft and cool it completely: warm onion starts cooking the meat.
Mix both minces with the panade, onion, egg, allspice and salt, and work it for five minutes until tacky.
Roll walnut-sized balls with wet hands and fry them in butter in batches, shaking the pan so they roll and colour evenly.
In the same pan whisk the flour into the remaining fat, pour in the stock and the rest of the cream, add the soy and cook five minutes to a sauce.
Return the meatballs to the sauce and warm them through for five minutes. Serve with mashed potato, lingonberry and pickled cucumber.

name: Mapo tofu
description: Tofu in a hot doubanjiang sauce with Sichuan pepper, which numbs rather than burns.

instructions.text: Slip the tofu into barely simmering salted water for three minutes and drain it gently.

Add the garlic, ginger and black beans, warm for half a minute and pour in the stock. Bring it to the boil.
Slide the tofu in and simmer for three minutes without stirring — swirl the pan instead, or the cubes break up.
Slake the cornflour in cold water and add it in two goes, letting the sauce come back to the boil each time. Off the heat, scatter over the ground Sichuan pepper and spring onion.

name: Mas huni
description: Tuna worked with coconut, onion and lime, with hot roshi flatbread. The Maldivian breakfast.

instructions.text: Knead a dough from the flour, water, a spoon of oil and salt and rest it twenty minutes.

Add the grated coconut and the flaked tuna and keep working it with your fingers until even.
Squeeze in the lime juice and mix again. Taste and adjust for salt and acidity.
Roll the dough into thin flatbreads and cook them on a dry pan a minute a side.
Serve the mas huni with the hot roshi and black tea.

description: Tanzanian fish curry on coconut milk with tamarind and curry powder.

Add the tomatoes and chilli and reduce them to a thick base without loose liquid.

name: Menemen
description: Eggs cooked into tomatoes and green pepper. They are never beaten and rarely stirred, or you end up with ordinary scrambled eggs.

instructions.text: Slice the peppers into rings and fry them in the two fats for three or four minutes, until the edges start to darken.
Add the tomatoes, salt them and cook over medium heat for ten minutes. Wait for the oil to separate and glisten at the edges — that is the sign the water has gone.
Lower the heat, break the eggs straight into the sauce and scatter the pepper flakes. Stir slowly and only two or three times, leaving streaks of yolk.
Take it off when the white has set and the yolk is still loose: the pan finishes the job. Scatter over the oregano and the cheese.

name: Misir wat
description: Red lentils in a berbere sauce. A fasting dish eaten in Ethiopia on fast days all year round.

instructions.text: Cook the onion dry in a pot for thirty minutes over medium heat, stirring, until it becomes a dark paste.
Pour in the oil, add the garlic and ginger and cook three minutes.
Stir in the berbere and tomato paste and fry five minutes: the mixture darkens and turns fragrant.
Add the lentils, pour in the water and simmer twenty-five minutes, stirring, until the lentils fall apart.
Season at the end, cook it down to a porridge-thick stew and serve with injera or flatbread.

name: Butter chicken
description: Yoghurt-marinated chicken, roasted, in a tomato and cream sauce finished with fenugreek.

instructions.text: Mix the yoghurt with half the ginger, garlic and spices, season it and marinate the chicken for at least an hour, better overnight.
Roast the chicken at 220 °C for twenty minutes, or sear it in a screaming-hot pan until it takes dark scorch marks. It can stay slightly underdone inside — the sauce will finish it.
Melt the butter and fry the onion with the rest of the ginger and garlic until golden. Add the tomatoes and the spices and cook for fifteen minutes.
Blend the sauce with the soaked cashews until completely smooth and return it to the pan. It is the cashews, not flour, that give the sauce its body.
Return the chicken to the sauce, pour in the cream and warm it through for five minutes without letting it boil. Crush the kasuri methi between your palms, stir it in and take the pan off.

name: Nikujaga
description: Beef and potato simmered in dashi with soy and mirin. The classic of Japanese home cooking.

instructions.text: Cut the potatoes into large pieces and soak them ten minutes in cold water to lose the surface starch.
Fry the onion in oil for two minutes, add the thinly sliced beef and cook until it loses its pink.
Add the potato and carrot and turn them so they take on the fat from the meat.
Add the dashi, sake and sugar, bring it up and skim.
Cover with an otoshibuta or a foil disc with a hole in it and simmer ten minutes over medium heat.
Add the soy and mirin and simmer fifteen minutes more, until only a little liquid is left at the bottom.
Add the beans for the last three minutes, take it off the heat and let it stand twenty minutes.

description: Minced pork fried with chilli, garlic and holy basil. Five minutes from start to plate.

instructions.text: Pound the garlic and chillies to a rough paste in a mortar. A mortar gives a different result from a knife: the juices come out and reach the oil.

name: Paella valenciana
description: Rice in a wide pan with chicken, rabbit and beans. It is never stirred once, and the crust on the bottom depends on that.

food.name: Bomba rice, or another short grain

ingredient_labels: bomba rice, or another short grain

instructions.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan and brown the chicken and rabbit on every side. This is not a five-minute job: it takes a good quarter of an hour, and there is no point rushing it — the flavour of the whole dish is laid down here.
Push the meat to the edges, put the green beans in the middle and fry them for a couple of minutes. Add the grated tomato and the paprika and cook until the tomato darkens and stops smelling raw.
Pour in the stock, add the rosemary, saffron and white beans, salt it noticeably harder than feels right and let it boil for ten minutes. This is the last moment you can correct the seasoning.
Scatter the rice in an even layer and level it once with a spoon. After that do not touch the pan again — no stirring, no smoothing.
Cook on a high flame for ten minutes, then drop to medium for another eight, until the stock is gone. The rice should be showing above the surface.
Turn the heat up for half a minute and listen: the moment the sound turns from bubbling to a dry crackle, take it off. That is the socarrat. Cover with a cloth and let it stand for five minutes.

name: Palak paneer
description: Spinach blanched and blended, with cubes of paneer. Spinach must not be stewed or it goes brown.

instructions.text: Drop the spinach into boiling water for ninety seconds and move it straight into iced water. Squeeze it out and blend it with the chilli to a purée.

Fry the cumin seeds in the ghee until they crackle, add the onion and cook it gold, then the ginger and garlic for a minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook seven minutes, until they break down and the fat starts separating at the edges.
Stir in the spinach purée, garam masala and salt, and warm it for exactly a minute. Add the paneer and cream and take it off the heat.

description: Chicken braised in caramelised sugar with vegetables, the Dominican weekday lunch.

description: Whole sardines salted coarsely and grilled over coals, served on a slice of bread.

Shake the excess salt off the fish and lay them on a hot, oiled grate.
Grill four minutes a side, turning them exactly once.
Lay the sardines on slices of bread and serve with boiled potatoes and the pepper salad.

name: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a thick sauce of tomato and pepper with cumin and paprika.

instructions.text: Fry the onion and peppers in the oil for ten minutes, until the pepper is soft and sweet.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and harissa and warm them for a minute — to the smell, not to burning.
Pour in the tomatoes, crush them and simmer for fifteen minutes. The sauce is ready when a spoon leaves a track on the bottom.
Make hollows with a spoon and break an egg into each. Cover and give it five to seven minutes: the whites set, the yolks stay loose.
Scatter over the feta and coriander and serve it in the pan with bread.

name: Skyr with berries
description: Home-made skyr, the Icelandic cultured dairy, strained thick, with bilberries.

instructions.text: Heat the milk to 85 °C, stirring, and hold it ten minutes without letting it boil.
Cool the milk to 40 °C by standing the pot in cold water.
Slacken the starter with a ladle of the warm milk and stir it back into the pot.
Add the rennet, stir for a few seconds and cover the pot.
Leave it somewhere warm for twelve hours, until the mass sets into a firm curd.
Turn the curd into a cloth and hang it over a bowl for six hours to drain the whey.
Whisk the skyr smooth and serve it with bilberries, cream and oats.

name: Smørrebrød
description: An open sandwich on rye with butter. The order of the layers and the thickness of the butter both matter.

instructions.text: Butter every slice right to the edges. The layer should be visible to the eye rather than translucent.
For herring: a lettuce leaf, then pieces of herring, onion rings and capers. The lettuce keeps the brine off the bread.
For prawns: lay them in tight overlapping rows, then a spoon of mayonnaise, a slice of lemon and dill.
For egg: overlapping rounds of boiled egg, a line of mayonnaise, dill and a pinch of salt over the top.
Serve at once, with a knife and fork. Smørrebrød is not picked up by hand; it is not built for that.

name: Souvlaki
description: Pork on skewers in lemon, oregano and olive oil, cooked fast over a fierce heat.

instructions.text: Mix the oil, lemon juice and zest, oregano, crushed garlic, salt and pepper. Coat the meat and leave it two hours, and no more than four.
While it marinates, make the tzatziki: yoghurt with the squeezed cucumber, a clove of garlic, a spoon of oil and salt.
Thread the meat onto skewers loosely — the heat has to get between the pieces. A tightly packed skewer stays raw in the middle.
Cook on a hot grill or griddle, three minutes on each of the four sides. The meat should darken rather than pale.
Rest the meat for five minutes, warm the pitas thirty seconds a side, and serve with the tzatziki and lemon.

name: Spaghetti carbonara
description: Pasta from four ingredients: guanciale, eggs, pecorino and pepper. There is no cream in it and never was.

ingredients.note: cut into short strips; pancetta works

instructions.text: Bring a large pot of water to the boil and salt it properly — this is the only salt in the dish, since the cheese and the guanciale bring their own.
Put the guanciale into a cold pan and turn the heat to medium. The fat should render gradually and the pieces turn golden and crisp at the edges, about 6 to 8 minutes.
While the fat renders, beat the yolks, the whole egg, the grated pecorino and the pepper into a thick paste. Let it sit at room temperature so it does not seize when it meets hot pasta.
Cook the spaghetti a minute short of the packet time. Before draining, save a cup of the cooking water — the sauce will not come together without it.
Take the pan off the heat, add the pasta and toss it through the fat. Let the pan cool for twenty seconds — it should be warm, not hot.
Pour in the egg mixture and stir hard, adding pasta water a spoonful at a time until the sauce turns glossy and coats every strand. Serve immediately.

name: Syrniki
description: Curd cheese fritters with as much curd as possible and exactly enough flour to keep them together.

ingredients.note: plus a little for your hands

instructions.text: Push the curd through a sieve or blitz it. Grainy curd makes grainy syrniki; this step is not optional.
Work in the egg, sugar, vanilla and salt, then the flour. The mixture stays sticky; that is correct.
With wet or lightly floured hands shape discs about a centimetre and a half thick. Thicker and the middle stays raw, thinner and they dry out.
Fry over medium heat with a lid on, three or four minutes a side. The lid matters more than the butter: it steams the middle through.

name: Toast Skagen
description: Prawns in a dill mayonnaise on fried bread, with roe on top.

instructions.text: Drain the prawns in a sieve and let them sit for at least ten minutes.
Mix the mayonnaise with the crème fraîche, chopped dill, horseradish, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Chop the red onion as fine as you can and stir it into the dressing.
Fold the prawns into the dressing gently, taking care not to crush them.
Trim the crusts from the bread and fry the slices in butter until browned on both sides.
Pile the prawns onto each toast, top with a spoon of roe and a sprig of dill. Serve at once.

name: Whitebait fritters
description: Whitebait bound with egg and fried as a thin cake, with lemon and nothing else.

instructions.text: Rinse the whitebait in cold water and drain it in a sieve for ten minutes.
Pat the whitebait dry with a cloth; excess water stops the fritter setting.
Whisk the eggs with the flour, salt and pepper until smooth and lump-free.
Fold the whitebait into the egg mixture gently, taking care not to crush it.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat until it just sizzles.
Pour in a ladle of the mixture and spread it into a thin round a centimetre thick.
Fry a minute and a half a side and serve with lemon and buttered bread.

name: Yangzhou fried rice
description: Rice with prawns, ham and egg, where every grain stays separate under a thin film of egg.

instructions.text: Separate two yolks and rub them through the cold rice with your hands until every grain is coated. Beat the remaining eggs separately.
Heat the wok with a spoon of oil until it smokes, pour in the beaten eggs, let them set and break them into pieces. Set them aside.
Fry the prawns for ninety seconds, add the ham, carrot and peas and cook a minute more. Add them to the eggs.
Add the rest of the oil, tip in the rice and fry three minutes at full heat, tossing constantly. The grains should be jumping in the wok, not sitting in it.
Return everything to the wok, pour the wine down the side and add the soy, season and toss for thirty seconds more. Scatter over the spring onion.
